tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of arXiv papers on RL for LLMs and agents, plus one AWS guide, not one developing story. Since Oct 23 it has collected work on rollout cost, RAG calibration and agent harnesses, and two studies showing that fine-grained credit and multi-turn RL gains depend on the setup.
whats_new: Nov 10: AutoScaffold argues RLVR's outcome reward shrinks each attempt to a single number and proposes AI-guided training-time scaffolds; Nov 9's MaxIM applies RL to bounded-memory summarization of long interaction histories.
why_it_matters: Agent RL results are sensitive to rollout budget, numerical setup and reward granularity, so a reported gain may not transfer to your harness. All are paper-reported, not production evidence.

beats.headline: Rollout scheduling and numerical stability set the cost of agent RL
beats.summary: Environment-aware and asynchronous rollout scheduling, BF16 rounding alignment, and a managed SageMaker recipe.

beats.headline: RL recipes tie confidence to correctness for RAG and knowledge tasks
Two studies find agent RL gains depend on credit granularity and interaction limits
beats.summary: Fine-grained credit can fail in video editing; multi-turn gains shift with sampling breadth K and interaction depth.

beats.headline: Error-targeted training, co-evolved harnesses and skill routing for tool agents
Neighboring RL work: simulation, robustness, explainability, compression, diffusion and world models
Newest papers try to recover training signal a single outcome reward discards
beats.summary: MaxIM targets credit assignment for memory updates; AutoScaffold adds AI-guided scaffolds to RLVR training.

open_questions: Do the multi-turn RL findings hold when sampling breadth and interaction depth are fixed to your production limits?
Do the credit-assignment findings from video editing hold on text-only tool-use agents?
Does co-evolving the harness with the policy beat a fixed harness on independent tasks?
Do gains from training-time scaffolds like AutoScaffold persist once the scaffold is removed at inference?
Does RL-trained incremental summarization like MaxIM beat a prompted summarizer on agent tasks outside its own benchmarks?
take_for_builders: Before adopting any of these recipes, rerun them at your own sampling breadth and turn limits, and A/B fine-grained credit or scaffolded rewards against episode-level reward; treat all results as unreplicated.
